Who is credited with discovering Zirconium?
Zirconium: Martin Heinrich Klaproth. Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
Who is credited with discovering Quetzalcoatlus?
Quetzalcoatlus: Douglas A. Lawson. Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon carbide?
Silicon carbide: Edward Goodrich Acheson. Silicon carbide (SiC), also known as carborundum, is a hard chemical compound of silicon and carbon.
Who is credited with discovering Bromine?
Bromine: Carl Jacob Löwig. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.

A German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the theory of relativity, his mass–energy formula E=mc2 comes from special relativity and has been called "the world's most famous equation." Born in 1879, who won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 - 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.

Affecting roughly 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder impairs the nervous system, causing severe intellectual disability and little to no speech, but is also linked to an unusually happy demeanor — what's it called?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.

This type of blood vessel typically carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, though the vessels serving the lungs and an unborn baby's placenta carry deoxygenated blood instead — what's it called?
Artery (from Greek (artr)) is a blood vessel in humans and most other animals that takes oxygenated blood away from the heart in the systemic circulation to one or more parts of the body.
Found in almost every habitat except the open sea and the poles, the order Coleoptera is the largest of all and accounts for about a quarter of every known animal species — which insects are these?
Beetle are insects that form the order Coleoptera, in the superorder Holometabola.
The third-most-produced bomber in history, this American four-engine heavy bomber dominated the European Theater and dropped more bombs than any other plane in WWII — which aircraft is it?
Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
This Indian physicist discovered, with his student, that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material — a phenomenon now named for him — earning a 1930 Nobel Prize. Who is he?
C. V. Raman (7 November 1888 - 21 November 1970) was an Indian physicist known for his work in the field of light scattering.
Belonging to the trumpet-vine family Bignoniaceae, this tree genus thrives across warm parts of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what is it called?
Catalpa is a genus of flowering plants in the family Bignoniaceae, native to warm temperate and subtropical regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia.
Native to East Asia and blooming late in the season, these autumn flowers of the daisy family are associated in the Northern Hemisphere with the month of November. What flower is it?
Chrysanthemum (kriss-), sometimes abbreviated to mums or chrysanths, are perennial herbaceous flowering plants in the family Asteraceae that bloom in the autumn.
Known by a colorful nickname, this inflammation of the clear layer over the white of the eye turns it pink, may leave it stuck shut by morning, and spreads easily — what is it?
Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva, the thin and clear layer that covers the white surface of the eye and the inner eyelid.

Known for names like thornapple, jimsonweed, and devil's trumpet, this genus of nine extremely poisonous, night-blooming plants in the nightshade family can cause hallucinations and delirium if ingested — what is it?
Datura is a genus of nine species of highly poisonous, vespertine-flowering plants belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).

Its name comes from a Greek word meaning 'deed' or 'act,' and Aristotle's Poetics contrasted it with the epic and lyric modes; two masks for comedy and tragedy are its emblem. What mode of fiction is it?
Drama is the specific mode of fiction represented in performance: a play, opera, mime, ballet, etc., performed in a theatre, or on radio or television.
Noted for producing one of the most variable litter sizes of any dog breed, this active gun dog comes in 'field' and 'house' varieties and gave rise to its American cousin breed — what is it?
English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.
Immature at birth but developed by puberty, this network of organs includes the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes, protected by a fold called the labia majora — what's it called?
Female reproductive system is made up of the internal and external sex organs that function in the reproduction of new offspring.
This Canadian physician and author has written five books exploring how childhood trauma shapes conditions from ADHD to addiction, arguing recovery must address underlying emotional pain — who is he?
Gabor Maté (born January 1944) is a Canadian physician and author.
This term describes the overall system of processes, rules, and power structures that sets boundaries of conduct and steers the direction of an organized group — what is it?

Governance is the overall complex system or framework of processes, functions, structures, rules, laws and norms born out of the relationships, interactions, power dynamics and communication within an organized group of individuals.

His synergy with information-theory father Claude Shannon laid foundations for the Information Age, and during WWII he helped build automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was this Dutch-American control-theory pioneer?
Hendrik Wade Bode (-d,; December 24, 1905 - June 21, 1982) was an American engineer, researcher, inventor, author and scientist, of Dutch ancestry.
Often caused by kidney failure or certain blood-pressure medications, this condition means too much potassium in the blood, with levels above 5.5 mmol/L — what's it called?
Hyperkalemia is an elevated level of potassium (K+) in the blood.
With the formula Fe2O3, this reddish inorganic compound occurs naturally as the mineral hematite, a key raw material for the steel industry — which compound?
Iron(III) oxide is the inorganic compound with the formula Fe2O3. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
Famed first for studying diamagnetism, which Irish physicist proved in 1859 the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect?
John Tyndall (2 August 1820 - 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.

Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine and beloved in Singapore and Malaysia, this spicy noodle dish swims in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind, topped with prawns or chicken — what's its name?
Laksa is a spicy noodle dish popular in Southeast Asia.
Named from the Greek word for 'stone,' this alkali metal with symbol Li tarnishes from silver to black in air and was once mined mainly from pegmatite minerals — what is it?
Lithium (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 32 to 57 deciduous trees and shrubs in the rose family includes the ancestors of a familiar orchard fruit plus ornamental wild and crab varieties — what's the genus?
Malus (or) is a genus of about 32-57 species of small deciduous trees or shrubs in the family Rosaceae, including the domesticated orchard apple, crab apples, and wild apples.
Together with the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, this monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe's fighter force throughout the Second World War. What aircraft is it?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Also called Indian mulberry, this tropical fruit tree contains harmful anthraquinones, and its foul-smelling fruit is mostly eaten only as a famine food — which species is it?
Morinda citrifolia is a fruit-bearing tree in the coffee family, Rubiaceae.
This multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves — their function and their disorders — blending physiology, anatomy, and more — name the field?
Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system (the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system), its functions, and its disorders.
Its name means 'serpent-bearer' in Ancient Greek — this large constellation straddling the celestial equator is depicted as a man grasping a snake — name it?
Ophiuchus (o-fee-) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This English amateur astronomer joined an astronomy association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's record-breaking 'The Sky at Night' — who was he?
Patrick Moore (4 March 1923 - 9 December 2012) was an English amateur astronomer who attained prominence in that field as a writer, researcher, radio commentator and television presenter.

This branch of linguistics studies how languages organize their foundational sound units — like the contrast between 'bat' and 'gnat' — or, in sign languages, elements like hand shape and location — what is it called?
Phonology (formerly also phonemics or phonematics) is the branch of linguistics that concerns how languages organize the foundational elements that make their words.
Native to cool temperate regions of the Old World, which poplar species is commonly known as European or quaking aspen?
Populus tremula (commonly called aspen, common aspen, Eurasian aspen, European aspen, or quaking aspen) is a species of poplar native to cool temperate regions of the Old World.
This kidney inflammation, most often caused by E. coli infection, typically causes fever and tenderness along the side of the body — what is it?
Pyelonephritis is inflammation of the kidney, typically due to a bacterial infection.
Made up of a large and small subunit built from RNA and proteins, this molecular machine found in every living cell translates messenger RNA into chains of amino acids — what is it?
Ribosome is a ribonucleoprotein particle found in all cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic, responsible for the synthesis of proteins.
Nicknamed the seven-year itch, this contagious skin condition is caused by a microscopic burrowing mite and thrives in crowded places like prisons and care homes — what is it?
Scabies (also sometimes known as the seven-year itch) is a contagious human skin infestation by the tiny (0.2-0.45 mm) mite Sarcoptes scabiei, variety hominis.
With the formula AgNO3, this colorless, highly water-soluble compound is the least expensive salt of a lustrous precious metal and a precursor to many similar compounds — name it?
Silver nitrate is an inorganic compound with chemical formula AgNO3.
Defined as exactly 101,325 pascals and roughly equal to Earth's average sea-level air pressure, what is this reference unit of pressure called?
Standard atmosphere (unit) (symbol: atm) is a unit of pressure defined as 101325 Pa.
Appointed a government economic minister in 1991, this academic rose to become prime minister of Turkey in 1993 and later served as its foreign minister — who is she?
Tansu Çiller (born 24 May 1946) is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996.

Proposing an information management system in March 1989 and implementing the first successful client-server exchange that November, this English computer scientist invented HTML, HTTP and the URL system — who is he?
Tim Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955), also known as TimBL, is an English computer scientist best known as the inventor of the World Wide Web, HTML, the URL system, and HTTP.
Lined with a type of tissue called transitional epithelium, this narrow tube can develop kidney stones or reflux problems and connects each kidney to the bladder — what is it?
Ureter are tubes composed of smooth muscle that transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.

First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass genus is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop, with varieties including spelt, durum, and einkorn — name the crop?
Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Struck off the medical register for 'serious professional misconduct,' this former surgeon authored the fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper falsely tying the MMR vaccine to autism — who is he?
This inflammatory condition causes right lower abdominal pain and is commonly triggered by a blockage from a calcified mass of feces called a fecalith — what is it?
Known medically as tinea pedis, this common fungal infection often begins between the toes and spreads in places like swimming pools and locker rooms — what is it?
Athlete's foot: Skin infection caused by fungus.
Commonly known as rays, this division of cartilaginous fish is instantly recognizable by its flattened body and enlarged pectoral fins fused to the head — what's it called?
Batomorphi: Division of cartilaginous fishes. Batomorphi, along with the shark division Selachii, both compose the subclass Elasmobranchii.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
Also nicknamed 'starflower,' this Mediterranean annual herb yields seed oil despite containing small amounts of toxic alkaloids — which plant?
Borage: Species of flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
Caused by heat, electricity, chemicals, friction, or radiation — and most often the result of scalding at home — what type of skin injury is classified from first- to higher-degree severity?
Burn: Injury to flesh or skin, often caused by excessive heat.
Produced by chili peppers likely to deter hungry mammals, this hydrophobic compound is what gives them their burning, pungent kick — what is it?
Capsaicin: Pungent chemical compound in chili peppers. It is a potent irritant for mammals for which it produces a sensation of burning in any tissue with which it comes into contact.

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
This French inventor born near Toulouse is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer, but in 1870 he was also among the first to take up the sport of cycling in France — who is it?
Clément Ader: French inventor and engineer (1841–1925)

Native to Europe and North Africa, this member of the carrot family can grow to 8 feet tall, with hollow stems blotched dark maroon and a distinctly foul smell carried on the wind — which highly poisonous plant is this?
Conium maculatum: Poisonous plant. The plant is herbaceous, with no woody parts, and has a biennial lifecycle.
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across India, Nepal, and southern China, this plant comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber: Species of flowering plant with edible fruits.

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
This natural anticoagulant boosts the activity of antithrombin and is used to prevent clotting during dialysis and in blood test tubes — what medication is it?
Heparin: Anticoagulant. Heparin, also known as unfractionated heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.

This American physicist dared to drop the wave-function-collapse postulate, proposing a 'relative state' theory that became the basis of the many-worlds interpretation — largely ignored until quantum decoherence vindicated him. Who is he?

Extracted from a Central African plant sacred to Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this hallucinogenic alkaloid was once marketed in Europe as a stimulant before being studied for other therapeutic uses — what is it?
Ibogaine: Psychoactive substance found in plants in the family Apocynaceae.
Awarded the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics, this British scientist discovered in 1897 that cathode rays were made of what we now call electrons — who is he?
Credited with popularizing the index fund, this investor founded The Vanguard Group and preached long-term patience over speculation — who is he?
John C. Bogle: American investor and business magnate (1929–2019)
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
This probability principle explains why a casino might lose money on a single spin of roulette but reliably earns a predictable percentage over many thousands of spins. What is it called?
Law of large numbers: Averages of repeated trials converge to the expected value.
Patented in 1978 and approved for use in the US in 1987, this ACE inhibitor is a common first-line treatment for high blood pressure — what drug is it?
Lisinopril: Medication used to treat hypertension and heart failure.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.

Raising silkworms at 13 and publishing a two-volume study of caterpillars, this German-Dutch artist was among the earliest European naturalists to document insects from direct observation — who was she?
Maria Sibylla Merian: German naturalist and artist (1647–1717)
Also called pennyroyal, this minty flowering plant native to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East has a folk-remedy history despite being toxic to the liver — what species is it?

Given the NATO reporting name 'Hip,' this Soviet-designed helicopter family has been in continuous production since 1975 as a medium twin-turbine transport, with an armed gunship variant — which aircraft?
Mil Mi-17: Family of Russian military transport helicopters.

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Colloquially known as a moon, this type of astronomical body orbits a planet or dwarf planet, with 455 confirmed examples across the Solar System's six major systems — what is it called?
Natural satellite: Astronomical body that orbits a planet. Natural satellites are colloquially referred to as moons, by analogy with the Moon, Earth's natural satellite.
Made from red algae and dried into flat sheets through a process resembling papermaking, this ingredient has wrapped sushi and rice balls in Japan since the 700s — what is it?
Nori: Edible seaweed species of the red algae genus Pyropia.
This medical specialty trains physicians for four years after medical school to diagnose, medically treat, and surgically correct eye disease — what is it?
Ophthalmology: Field of medicine treating eye disorders.
Credited as the 'father of toxicology,' this Swiss Renaissance physician and alchemist also wrote prophetic 'Prognostications' later studied by Rosicrucians — who is he?
Paracelsus: Swiss physician, philosopher, theologian, and alchemist (c. 1493 – 1541)
Its rows are called periods and its columns are called groups, and it arranges the chemical elements so that their properties recur as atomic number rises. What is this icon of chemistry?

The periodic table arranges the chemical elements into rows called periods and columns called groups. It depicts the periodic law: arranged by atomic number, the elements show an approximate recurrence of properties.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
This evergreen shrub or small tree native to South America is pollinated chiefly by the honey bee and gives us a popular tropical fruit — what species is it?
Psidium guajava: Species of flowering plant.
Born from refraction, internal reflection, and dispersion of light in water droplets, this arc always appears in the patch of sky directly opposite the sun — what is it?
Made of a large and small subunit built from RNA and protein, which cellular structure translates messenger RNA into chains of amino acids?
Ribosome: Macromolecular machine that synthesizes proteins in cells.

Built by a Swedish manufacturer, this single-engine fighter was the first mass-produced canard-design aircraft and the first with a digital avionics computer, unsurpassed until the Tornado arrived in 1981 — which jet?
Saab 37 Viggen: 1967 Swedish fighter aircraft family.
Native to cold-temperate Eurasia, this spiny deciduous shrub yields a fruit and oil prized in both cooking and cosmetics — what plant is it?
Sea buckthorn: Species of flowering plant in the family Elaeagnaceae.

Also called carborundum, this hard compound occurs in nature as the rare mineral moissanite but has been mass-produced as an abrasive since 1893 — and it stiffens disc brakes and bulletproof vests; what is it?
Silicon carbide: Wide-bandgap semiconductor and abrasion-resistant ceramic.
Known by nicknames like 'garden' and 'lamb,' and native from Ireland to southern China, which herb's aromatic oil flavors food, teas, and various scents?
Spearmint: Plant species in the mint family.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)
The symbol for seaborgium is Sg. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.

Amitabh Bachchan (né Srivastava; born 11 October 1942) is an Indian actor, playback singer, and producer who primarily works in Hindi cinema.
In what year did James Gandolfini die?
James Gandolfini: James John Gandolfini (Italian: [ɡandolˈfiːni]; September 18, 1961 – June 19, 2013) was an American actor.

Alien is a 1979 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Dan O'Bannon, based on a story by O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett.

Wonka is a 2023 musical fantasy film directed by Paul King, who co-wrote the screenplay with Simon Farnaby.

Madame Web is a 2024 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character.
In what year was Godzilla Minus One first released?
Godzilla Minus One: It is the 37th film in the Godzilla franchise, the 33rd film thereof produced by Toho, and the fifth installment in the Reiwa era.
In what year was Thor: The Dark World first released?
Thor: The Dark World: 2013. It is the sequel to Thor (2011) and the eighth film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).
In what year was Gayniggers from Outer Space first released?
Gayniggers from Outer Space is a 1992 English-language Danish satirical science fiction short film, directed by Danish performance artist Morten Lindberg.
In what year was X-Men: Apocalypse first released?
X-Men: Apocalypse: 2016. X-Men: Apocalypse is a 2016 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics superhero team the X-Men.

The Boss Baby is a 2017 American animated spy comedy film starring Alec Baldwin as the voice of the titular character.
